title: Bayesian Biomechanics
text:
Preface
Bayesian Biomechanics is an interactive introduction to Bayesian data analysis for biomechanics researchers. It assumes no prior experience with Bayesian statistics and only a little Python.

title: Bayesian Biomechanics
text:
How the book works
Each chapter combines prose with interactive marimo notebooks:

In the browser. Lessons that only need lightweight tools (NumPy, SciPy) run directly in your browser through WebAssembly. Nothing to install.
On your computer. Lessons that fit models with PyMC and Bambi run locally. The book shows their pre-computed results, and Appendix A — Running the lessons locally explains how to run them yourself.

title: Bayesian Biomechanics
text:
Further reading
Good general introductions to Bayesian data analysis include McElreath (2020) and Gelman et al. (2013).

title: Appendix A — Running the lessons locally
text:
A.1 Option 1: the whole book with pixi (recommended)
Lessons that run in the browser need no setup. For lessons that fit models with PyMC and Bambi, you need Python on your own computer. There are two ways to get it.
pixi installs Python and every package the book uses into a folder inside the project, without touching the rest of your system.
The lesson opens in your web browser.

title: Appendix A — Running the lessons locally
text:
Install pixi by following the installation instructions for your operating system.
Download the book’s code, either with git:
git clone https://github.com/jobindjohn/bayesian-biomechanics.git
cd bayesian-biomechanics
or by downloading and unzipping the ZIP archive.
Open a lesson. The first run downloads and installs everything, which can take a few minutes:
pixi run lesson 02-first-regression/first_regression.py



A.1.1 Re-fitting the models
Lessons load pre-computed results when they exist, so they open quickly. To fit the models again from scratch and overwrite the saved results:
pixi run refit 02-first-regression/first_regression.py

title: Appendix A — Running the lessons locally
text:
A.2 Option 2: a single notebook
Every notebook lists the packages it needs at the top of the file, so you can run one on its own. Download it with the button on the lesson’s page, install uv, and run:
uvx marimo edit --sandbox first_regression.py
uv reads the package list from the notebook and installs it into a private environment for that notebook.
